name: TT-Forge (Tenstorrent's MLIR-based compiler; the TT-Bridge / graph-frontend layer)
production_evidence: The vendor's own software-stack overview presents TT-Forge as the supported path to compile PyTorch, JAX and TensorFlow models for Tenstorrent hardware
The existing engines/niche-tt-metal record carries TT-Metalium/TT-NN throughput tables measured through this stack
strengths: MLIR-based, the same infrastructure Triton, IREE and XLA use, so pass and dialect work is shareable
Ingests three framework front ends (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow) plus ONNX rather than one
Lowers to TT-Metalium, so the graph compiler and the hand-written kernel layer compose instead of competing
Open source under Apache-2.0, which is unusual for a vendor compiler for non-x86 hardware
weaknesses: No target in this schema's vocabulary: Tenstorrent's RISC-V vector cores are not cuda/rocm/hip/tpu/metal or any listed value, so target_backends is empty rather than mislabelled - the enum has no slot for a vendor's own non-x86 accelerator

No output artifact in the enum either: TT-Forge emits TT-Metalium kernels and binaries, and amdgcn is recorded here only because it is the schema's stand-in for generated machine code, which is NOT what it emits. Treat both empty/approximate fields as enum debt
Vendor-generic by design: the vendor's own claim is 'an automated, general path ... without requiring custom kernel development', which is a statement about coverage, not about peak performance
No autotuning, so performance is bounded by whatever the operator library and the model happen to get
Younger and far smaller than Triton or XLA: 368 stars, 554 commits
notes: Added as the graph-compiler layer of the Tenstorrent stack that engines/niche-tt-metal covers from the kernel side, because a deployment planner choosing Tenstorrent needs both: TT-Forge to get a model down, TT-Metalium to write what it misses. The vendor's stack overview is unusually explicit about the boundaries - TT-Forge 'bridges high-level machine learning frameworks with the Tenstorrent software stack', TT-NN is the pre-packaged operator library, TT-Metalium is the low-level programming model - which is what makes the split record-able. The task framed this as 'TT-Bridge and TT-Metal'. TT-Metalium is already covered by engines/niche-tt-metal, so this record covers the compiler. On the 'TT-Bridge' name: the GitHub API has no tenstorrent/tt-bridge repository (404) and PyPI has no tt-bridge package (404), while tenstorrent/tt-forge exists, is described by its own repo as 'Tenstorrent's MLIR Based Compiler', and is the live project - so I recorded what exists rather than the name as given. It is plausible TT-Bridge is/was an internal or renamed frontend; the repo's own history would settle it, and I did not find a primary source either way, so no claim is made about the naming. output_artifacts carries amdgcn as a deliberate approximation and target_backends is empty: neither is accurate. TT-Forge emits TT-Metalium device binaries, and the schema's enums (built for CUDA/ROCm/Metal-class hardware) have no term for it. Both fields are recorded as-is rather than dropped, because leaving them empty loses the information that a real artifact is emitted somewhere - but a reader must not take amdgcn literally here. autotuning is false: nothing in the vendor's stack documentation describes a tactic search or config search in TT-Forge. If Tenstorrent adds one, this field is the thing to revisit.
